physics_goals.locator: HAPPEX collaboration home page, 'About The HAPPEX Collaboration'
physics_goals.quote: The main science program of the collaboration aimed at measuring the strange quark contribution to the electromagnetic properties of nucleons.
physics_goals.value: Measure the strange-quark contribution to the electromagnetic properties of the nucleon through parity-violating electron scattering

summary.plain: HAPPEX measured how electrons spinning one way or the other scatter slightly differently from hydrogen and helium nuclei in Jefferson Lab's Hall A. The difference reveals whether strange quarks, absent from a proton's three main quarks, contribute to its charge and magnetism: with the other experiments, to a few percent at most.
summary.technical: Parity-violating elastic electron scattering with polarised CEBAF beams in Hall A and the twin High Resolution Spectrometers with integrating detectors: HAPPEX-I (1998-1999, Q^2 = 0.477 (GeV/c)^2), HAPPEX-II and HAPPEX-He (2004-2005, Q^2 about 0.1 (GeV/c)^2, hydrogen and 4He targets) and HAPPEX-III (2009, 3.48 GeV, Q^2 = 0.624 GeV^2, A_PV = -23.80 +- 0.78 +- 0.36 ppm); strange form factors consistent with zero, bounded to a few percent of the proton's.
